paragraphs.text: At Richmond Pediatric Dentistry & Orthodontics we strive to deliver radiant, healthy smiles to families across Richmond, VA. Our kind and caring team is committed to providing professional, high-quality care in an environment that is relaxing and fun.

We take a patient-centered approach that blends specialized pediatric and orthodontic treatments with compassionate communication. Our goal is to make dental and orthodontic visits positive, comfortable, and achievable for every family.

Using modern techniques and a gentle touch, we offer tailored care for children, teens, and adults — from routine pediatric visits to braces and Invisalign<sup>®</sup> — so each patient leaves healthier and more confident.
We believe in building long-term relationships with families, supporting oral health through education, flexible scheduling, and community partnerships that make care easier to access.

Dr. Jayakumar Jayaraman, BDS, MDS, MS, PhD is a pediatric dentist with extensive training and a deep commitment to working with children. He brings a calm, patient-centered style to every visit and enjoys making dental care approachable and even fun for his youngest patients.

Dr. Jayaraman completed his Bachelor of Dental Surgery in Chennai, India, and earned a Master of Dental Surgery and Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Hong Kong. He also holds a Certificate in Pediatric Dentistry and a Master of Science in Pediatric Dentistry from the University of Texas Health San Antonio.

Outside the office Dr. Jayaraman enjoys traveling, trying new foods, cooking, and learning to fly. He brings warmth and a gentle approach to care, helping children feel safe and engaged during visits.

Dr. Payton Cook, DDS is a board-trained orthodontist who provides comprehensive orthodontic care for children, teens, and adults. She is known for a gentle, patient-focused style and a strong commitment to helping patients achieve confident, healthy smiles.

Dr. Cook earned a B.S. in Biomedical Sciences from the University of South Florida and her Doctor of Dental Surgery from VCU School of Dentistry. She completed her orthodontic certificate at the University of Texas Health Science Center at Houston.
Outside of work Dr. Cook enjoys family time, fitness, and running Richmond trails. She brings the same energy and attention to detail to patient care that she applies in her active personal life.
Dr. Sarah Yi, DDS is a pediatric dentist who focuses on creating positive, child-friendly dental experiences. She builds rapport with children and families to make visits relaxed and educational.

Dr. Yi completed a B.S. in Biology at Virginia Commonwealth University and earned her Doctor of Dental Surgery from VCU School of Dentistry. She completed her pediatric residency at Children’s Hospital Colorado.
Dr. Yi enjoys pottery, home decorating, and spending time with her husband and their two rescue pups. She finds great reward in connecting with children and helping them leave the office smiling.

Dr. Kevin Bibona, DDS is an orthodontist who enjoys guiding patients through their treatment journeys and seeing the confidence a finished smile brings. He combines clinical expertise with a friendly approach.
Dr. Bibona completed undergraduate studies at Washington and Lee University and earned his DDS and orthodontic certificate from VCU School of Dentistry.
When not working Dr. Bibona enjoys family life and coaching his children’s soccer teams. He values being part of the Richmond community and helping patients feel confident about their smiles.

Dr. Bill Dahlke, DMD is a pediatric dentist with nearly 20 years of experience. He focuses on making dental visits comfortable and enjoyable for children, building trusting relationships with families.
Dr. Dahlke studied biochemistry at the University of Nevada–Reno and received his Doctor of Dental Medicine (DMD) and pediatric dentistry training from UNLV School of Dental Medicine.
Outside the office Dr. Dahlke enjoys cooking, baking bread, working on cars, and spending time with his family. He brings warmth and humor to patient care.

Dr. Jasmine Chopra, DDS is a Richmond-native pediatric dentist who emphasizes teaching healthy habits and making dental visits enjoyable for kids. She focuses on building trust with both children and parents.

Dr. Chopra completed undergraduate studies at Virginia Commonwealth University, earned her DDS from the University of Minnesota School of Dentistry, and completed her certificate in Pediatric Dentistry at NYU Langone.
Dr. Chopra enjoys exploring Richmond, trying new foods, and spending time with family and friends. She is also learning French and values cultural awareness in care.

Dr. Raymonia Eddleton, DDS is a Richmond native and experienced pediatric dentist who takes pride in serving local families. She brings nearly 30 years of experience and a warm, patient-focused approach to care.

Dr. Eddleton completed undergraduate studies at Virginia Tech, earned her DDS from the University of Tennessee, and completed pediatric dentistry training at Cincinnati Children’s Hospital Medical Center.
Dr. Eddleton enjoys family time, exercise, and running with her Labradoodle. She loves the funny stories children share and the daily joy of working with young patients.
Dr. Rachel Thornton, DDS is a board-eligible pediatric dentist who is passionate about building positive, lasting relationships with families and helping children feel comfortable during visits.

Dr. Thornton earned a B.A. from Washington University in St. Louis and her DDS from Marquette University School of Dentistry. She completed pediatric dental training at Yale New Haven Hospital, serving as Chief Resident.
Originally from Madison, Dr. Thornton enjoys the beach, playing frisbee with her golden retriever, Louie, making playlists, and exploring interior design and fashion in her free time.

paragraphs.text: Your first visit at Richmond Pediatric Dentistry & Orthodontics is a friendly introduction: meet our team, get a complete oral exam with any needed X-rays, and talk through which care options fit your child.
We’ll review medical history, create a customized treatment plan, and explain insurance and payment options so you leave with a clear next step.

image.alt: Parent and child at a dental reception desk

Flexible payment options are available. Our treatment coordinators will review costs and help find a plan that works for your family.

paragraphs.text: Your child’s first dental visit should be early: the American Academy of Pediatric Dentistry recommends a checkup by age one or when the first tooth erupts. This early visit helps establish a dental home, build comfort with the dentist and introduce healthy habits. Our pediatric dentists are specially trained to care for children; they are compassionate, skilled and enjoy working with kids every day. A typical first visit may include an exam, a cleaning when appropriate, and guidance for at-home care.

At Richmond Pediatric Dentistry & Orthodontics, our restorative dentistry services help children keep strong, healthy smiles. From composite fillings and stainless steel crowns to pulpal therapy and space maintainers, we restore function and appearance with gentle, effective care tailored for young patients.

Pediatric dental sedation helps anxious or very young patients receive necessary care in a safe, controlled way. Options include nitrous oxide (laughing gas), oral sedatives and, when appropriate, in-office general anesthesia. Our team evaluates each child carefully, obtains parental consent, and monitors vital signs throughout treatment to ensure safety and comfort.
We explain preliminary evaluation steps, required consent, monitoring protocols and post-care instructions so parents know what to expect and how to support recovery.

Traditional metal braces remain a reliable option for a wide range of orthodontic needs. Brackets and archwires apply steady, controlled force to move teeth into healthier, more functional positions. They are durable, cost-effective and a strong choice for patients who prefer a fixed treatment.
Durable and cost-effective, metal braces use small brackets and wires to gradually move teeth into place.
Ceramic braces blend with tooth color for a less noticeable option while still delivering effective results.

image.alt: Patient smiling with discreet ceramic braces
Two stylish smiling teens taking a selfie with braces

paragraphs.text: Spark Clear Aligners are an advanced clear-aligner option that use TruGEN™ material to provide a more comfortable, clear and stain-resistant solution. Clear aligners allow you to brush and eat without bracket restrictions while treating a wide variety of orthodontic problems.

image.alt: Close-up of clear aligners being placed on teeth

paragraphs.text: Early orthodontic evaluation helps our team identify developing problems and plan conservative treatments that can shorten or simplify care later. Treating issues while a child’s bones are still growing often leads to gentler, faster results and can prevent more complex procedures in the future.

image.alt: Young patient receiving early orthodontic intervention

paragraphs.text: If a tongue-tie or lip tie affects feeding, speech or oral development, our team can evaluate and treat the issue. We perform lingual or labial frenectomies using a CO2 laser when appropriate; the procedure is quick, causes minimal bleeding and typically allows fast recovery so children can feed and use their tongue more freely.

Pulpal therapy preserves a badly decayed baby tooth by treating the damaged nerve tissue. Depending on the situation, a pulpotomy or pulpectomy may be performed to remove infected pulp and maintain the tooth until its natural replacement. This helps retain proper chewing function and space for the permanent tooth.

FAQ.title: Frequently Asked Questions For Orthodontic Emergencies

paragraphs.text: Properly handling an orthodontic emergency can be critical to maintaining your treatment progress and protecting your oral health. When unexpected issues arise, handling it effectively can make all the difference. We’ve compiled some of the most common orthodontic issues we see and their solutions below.

accordion.header: What should I do if a bracket or band becomes loose?

paragraphs.text: If a bracket or band comes loose but is still attached to the wire, try to leave it in place and apply orthodontic wax to reduce irritation. If it comes completely off, save the piece and bring it with you to your next appointment. Call (804) 740-7281 so the office can determine if it needs to be fixed sooner.

image.alt: Happy family portrait related to orthodontic care

accordion.header: How can I fix a wire that's poking or irritating my mouth?

paragraphs.text: Use a cotton swab or an eraser on a pencil to gently nudge the wire back into a more comfortable position. If that doesn’t work, place a small piece of orthodontic wax over the end of the wire to prevent it from poking. If it is still uncomfortable, call (804) 740-7281 or let the team know at your next appointment.

image.alt: Patient receiving guidance during orthodontic appointment

accordion.header: What do I do if a rubber band or color tie falls off?

paragraphs.text: If you notice a missing ligature (the small rubber band or wire that holds the bracket wire in place), call the office to see if it needs to be replaced. These ties help apply the correct pressure to your teeth, so the practice may recommend fixing it sooner rather than later.

image.alt: Orthodontic team collaborating to provide care

accordion.header: Is it normal to feel soreness after getting braces or having them adjusted? What can I do for relief?

paragraphs.text: This is completely normal. You may feel some discomfort for a few days after getting your braces on or following an adjustment. Rinsing with warm salt water, eating soft foods, and using over-the-counter pain relievers as necessary can help manage it.

image.alt: Patient comfort and relief after orthodontic adjustment

accordion.header: What can I do about mouth sores caused by braces?

paragraphs.text: Braces can irritate the inside of your cheeks or lips, especially early on in your treatment journey. Use orthodontic wax over any brackets causing discomfort and rinse with warm salt water to promote healing. If the sores don’t go away or worsen, contact the office at https://rpdo.com/contact-us/.

image.alt: Patient smiling after resolving mouth discomfort

accordion.header: Help! I think I swallowed part of my appliance.

paragraphs.text: While rare, this can happen. First, don’t panic. Call the office at (804) 740-7281 to request an appointment as soon as possible. Seek immediate medical assistance if you experience any trouble breathing.

image.alt: Orthodontic team ready to assist with appliance concerns

accordion.header: My retainer broke. Should I replace it?

paragraphs.text: Retention is an important phase of orthodontic treatment that protects your new smile. If your retainer breaks, the practice recommends getting a new one as soon as possible.

image.alt: Replacement retainer prepared by orthodontic team

accordion.header: When should I seek immediate care?

paragraphs.text: If you’ve experienced an orthodontic emergency involving trauma to the face, jaw or mouth (for example, a sports injury or fall), contact the office right away at (804) 740-7281. Even if appliances appear intact, the orthodontist may perform a thorough examination to rule out damage. Patients with jaw injury or heavy bleeding should go to the emergency room immediately.
